note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Leija C et al. Pyrimidine Salvage Enzymes Are Essential for De Novo Biosynthesis of Deoxypyrimidine Nucleotides in Trypanosoma brucei PLoS pathogens 2016.
pathway_in_one_line: The deoxypyrimidine interconversion cycle in Trypanosoma brucei, in which thymidine kinase, cytidine deaminase and a newly identified HD-domain 5'-nucleotidase together balance the dCTP, dUTP and dTTP pools.
scope_note: In scope: deoxycytidine -> deoxyuridine (CDA), thymidine -> dTMP and deoxyuridine -> dUMP (TK), dCMP -> deoxycytidine / dTMP -> thymidine / dUMP -> deoxyuridine (the HD-domain 5'-nucleotidase identified here), dUMP -> dTMP (thymidylate synthase with 5,10-methylene-THF), uridine -> uracil (UPP), and the heterologous rescue conversions dCMP -> dUMP (human DCTD) and dCTP -> dUTP. In scope as an explicit NEGATIVE: uridine phosphorylase does NOT convert uracil to deoxyuridine, which is the paper's argument for a missing enzyme. Adjacent: the six de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis steps, which the text names only by enzyme and EC number with the substrates in the Fig 1 scheme - a drafter must not book them as two-sided. Also adjacent: the transamination / methionine / acetyl-ornithine metabolomics digressions in the Discussion.
selected_because: The densest set of named two-sided conversions in the set, in a parasite, with a genuine negative result and a genuine missing-enzyme inference to test the review_required path. Longest paper chosen (109k chars) - accepted because the chemistry is concentrated in Fig 1 plus three Results sections and the rest is growth-rescue and metabolomics a drafter can scope out. This is the one paper in the set that duplicates an already-filled grid cell (metabolic chemistry x other); it was kept over a weaker paper in an empty cell.
